stops.name: Parthenon
stops.en: This massive temple was built in the 5th century BC in thanksgiving for the Greek victory over Persian invaders. It was later converted into a Christian church, then an Ottoman mosque. It was mostly intact until 1687, when a Venetian bomb landed on the Parthenon, which the Ottomans had used as a munitions dump. From 1800 to 1803, the 7th Earl of Elgin removed many of the surviving sculptures and s

stops.name: Acropolis of Athens
stops.en: It was the ancient fortified town of Athens, dating back to the Late Bronze Age. It is now a UNESCO World Heritage Site for its historic role and the many iconic buildings of the Greek Classical age, among them the Parthenon, the Erectheion, and the Temple of Athena Nike. The key landmark of Athens, visible from afar, the Acropolis dominates the Athenian sky and symbolizes the foundation of modern

stops.name: Erechtheion
stops.en: This elegant temple was primarily dedicated to the goddess Athena. The uneven ground led to a complex plan, with an east-facing entrance lined with six Ionic columns. Unusually, the temple has two porches, one borne by Ionic columns, the other supported by huge female caryatids.

stops.name: Panathenaic Stadium
stops.en: The stadium that housed the first modern day Olympic Games of 1896. Earlier versions of the stadium date as far back as 330 BCE. It's an enormous, white, marble stadium, with a horseshoe configuration.

stops.name: Temple of Hephaestus
stops.en: The best preserved ancient Greek temple, 5th century BCE.

stops.name: Temple of Olympian Zeus
stops.en: Only the ruins remain today. The column that has fallen and can still be seen in pieces was brought down during a thunderstorm about a century ago.

stops.name: Ancient Agora of Athens
stops.en: The site of the ancient city centre is a green space with a beautiful view of the Acropolis. It was built as a multipurpose area, then evolved into a religious area over time. The Ancient Agora was eventually abandoned and then large parts of it were later built over for a thousand years. The open space you see today was excavated starting in the 1850s.

stops.name: Theatre of Dionysus
stops.en: Classical Athens' main theatre, the first theatre ever built. Many of the great Greek plays were performed here for the first time. According to Plato's Symposium, it could hold an audience of 19,000 spectators. Aristophanes' The Clouds, mocking Socrates, was first performed here, and Plato considered this play to be a contributing factor in Socrates' trial and execution.

stops.name: Odeon of Herodes Atticus
stops.en: This theatre, built in 161 CE, is still used for concerts and plays. The stone backdrop is still preserved to a remarkable height of 3 stories, because it was incorporated into a later fortification on the site.

stops.name: Kerameikos
stops.en: The site of the ancient cemetery of Athens. It also houses the Dipylon Gate, where the Panathenaic procession would begin. Its museum showcasing many of the grave stele and other archaeological items found on the grounds. The site has more than 20 tortoises, so be sure to watch your step and not trample on them.

stops.name: Pnyx
stops.en: If Athens is the birthplace of democracy, then Pnyx is its cradle. Around 507 BCE this rocky hill, overlooking the Akropolis, became the meeting place for the ekklesia, Athens' early democratic assembly. This site thus witnessed addresses by Pericles, Aristides and Alcibiades during the "Golden Age" of Athens, and had a capacity for 6000 to 13,000 hearers. The site was redesigned several times, cr

stops.name: Stoa of Attalos
stops.en: This building was reconstructed in the 1950s from its original foundations, incorporating as much of the original structure and materials as possible, with limestone quarried from Piraeus and roof tiles made of clay from Attica. It is used as a museum to house relics found in the Agora.

stops.name: Propylaea of Athens
stops.en: The monumental gate at the western end of the Acropolis with Doric columns of Pentelic marble. In a prominent position on a steep bastion to the right of the entrance is the Temple of Athena Nike

stops.name: Platonic Academy
stops.en: This house of study was founded by the famous philosopher Plato. His equally famous follower Aristotle studied here for 20 years before leaving to found a school of his own. The site is an outdoor free park where you can see the excavated ruins. The ruins are not well explained or particularly impressive, but they do form a very nice park in a charming family oriented neighborhood. The exact coord

stops.name: Daphni Monastery
stops.en: An 11th-century Byzantine monastery and UNESCO World Heritage site. Damaged by an earthquake in 1999, but has now been fully restored.

stops.name: National Archaeological Museum of Athens
stops.en: This is the largest and most popular of Athens' many museums, and is usually very crowded. Its vast collection includes treasures unearthed from Mycenae by Heinrich Schliemann; a staggering array of sculpture including the earliest known Greek figurines dating from around 2,000 BCE; frescoes from the volcanic island of Santorini; and remains of Antikythera mechanism, the oldest known mechanical co

stops.name: Mount Lycabettus
stops.en: A 200m hill bordering the Kolonaki district. You can reach the top by walking (the path starts 15 minutes from Evangelismos metro stop, and will take 30 minutes to walk up the winding, but paved and not steep, path) or by a funicular railway (€10 single/€13 return trip). From halfway up looking towards the sea there are astonishing views of the Parthenon with the blue of the sea glimpsed between i

stops.name: Acropolis Museum
stops.en: You will need to purchase a timed-entry ticket for this museum, separate from the Acropolis. Buying online in advance from the official website is strongly recommended. This museum replaces an older museum on the Acropolis, which was far too small to hold and display all the artifacts recovered by archaeologists. Its design looks very "modern" from the outside, but on the inside it's very intuitiv

stops.name: Syntagma Square
stops.en: Check out the Parliament building and the newly restored Grande Bretagne Hotel.

stops.name: Benaki Museum
stops.en: Visit the beautiful Neoclassical main building which houses collections of Greek art, from ancient times through the Byzantine period and the modern state. Open late and for free on Thursday evenings. The museum shop is a good place to buy souvenirs. There is a small selection at high prices but the quality is excellent.

stops.name: Arch of Hadrian
stops.en: A monumental gateway resembling a Roman triumphal arch. It was built around 131 AD to honor the Roman emperor Hadrian, an admirer of Greek culture, for his many benefactions to the city.

stops.name: Church of the Holy Apostles
stops.en: From the 11th century, one of the oldest churches in Athens.

stops.name: Roman Agora of Athens
stops.en: This area became the main marketplace of the city after the Ancient Agora to the west became primarily a religious facility under Roman rule. It houses the Tower of the Winds, an eight-sided tower with a different wind deity on each side, the remains of ancient shops, and a fountain. Although the official entrance faces the end of Pikilis, you cannot buy tickets at the entrance. The ticket office

stops.name: Kaisariani monastery
stops.en: A nice escape from the city in the foothills of Mount Hymettus. Walking trails. There's a functional monastery one can walk in, and several ruined chapels or basilicas up on the walks.

stops.name: Tomb of the Unknown Soldier, Athens
stops.en: Catch the changing of the guards in front of the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier in front of Parliament every hour on the hour. The guards are a fascinating sight; they wear distinctive uniforms with pleated kilts and leather clogs with pom-poms. The uniforms and the guards' unusual marching style are a tribute to the light infantry insurgents (evzones) who bravely fought the Greek War of Independence

stops.name: Lyceum
stops.en: An ancient temple here hosted lectures by Socrates, Plato, and Aristotle, and early meetings of the Athenian Assembly. Aristotle made the temple the home of his school, the Lyceum. It hosted the world's first zoo and botanical garden, as well as a library which preserved classical Greek works for centuries afterwards. Rediscovered in 1996, the site can now be viewed outdoors. Entrance is from the

stops.name: Museum of Cycladic Art
stops.en: Holds the second largest collection of Cypriot antiquities in the world outside Cyprus, after the Metropolitan Museum in New York. Some of the most popular exhibits include the Cycladic figurines, the idols from Early Bronze Age Cyclades, whose style greatly influenced modernist work in the 20th century, and Cypriot pottery and Ancient Greek artifacts, especially the ‘Scenes of Daily Life in Ancie

stops.name: National Historical Museum
stops.en: In the old parliament building, this museum contains a large collection of historic documents such as the first constitution of Greece, furniture, equipment from the revolution. If you are lucky you may see the old session room.

stops.name: Numismatic Museum of Athens
stops.en: The building of the museum is one of the most beautiful in Athens, and was built by Ernst Ziller and was used as the residence in Athens of Schliemann. The collection contains thousands of ancient coins and ancient Greek, Roman, Byzantine, Medieval figurines.

stops.name: National Gallery of Athens
stops.en: It's one of Greece's main art institutions and features paintings and works of art from some of Greece's and Europe's best from the 19th and 20th centuries. Emphasis is given to popular Greek contemporary artists including Giannis Tsarouchis, Domenikos Theotokopoulos (a.k.a. El Greco), Theodors Vrizakis, Nikolaos Kounelakis, Nikiforos Litras, Konstantinos Parthenis, Maleas, Giannis Moralis and oth

stops.name: Athens War Museum
stops.en: The National War Museum is the only significant surviving public project of the military dictatorship which ruled Greece 1967 - 1974. The museum's displays are old fashioned and biased towards the more successful periods of Greek military history. The tanks, artillery guns and aircraft on display outside the museum form the most interesting part of its collection, and can be visited for free. Perh

stops.name: National Theatre of Greece - Ziller Building
stops.en: A low but imposing building erected between 1882 and 1890 by architect Ernst Ziller in the eclectic style of that age, commissioned by King George I.

stops.name: Paul and Alexandra Canellopoulos Museum
stops.en: A small but excellent museum displays artifacts from Mycenean Greece on, and includes some wonderful Persian artifacts.

stops.name: Museum of Greek Folk Musical Instruments
stops.en: Includes exhibits of traditional Greek musical instruments, with recordings of most of them.

stops.name: Technopolis City of Athens
stops.en: An industrial museum of incomparable architecture. The centre has assisted in the upgrading of a historic Athens district.

stops.name: Vorres Museum
stops.en: A museum of folk and contemporary art. Its grounds cover 320,000 m2 (80 acres) including several buildings, gardens and courtyards. Its collection includes over 6,000 pieces covering 4,000 years of Greek history and art. The museum was donated by the Vorres family to the Greek state.

stops.name: Museum of Greek Folk Art
stops.en: An excellent museum of its type. Too often neglected by visitors to Athens, even though it is in the heavily touristed Plaka neighbourhood. Displays include artefacts, tools, primitive painting, folk pottery and interior decor. It is particularly strong on costume and embroidery.

stops.name: Municipal Gallery of Athens
stops.en: Paintings of Greek painters of the first half of the 20th century are displayed.

stops.name: Hadrian's Reservoir
stops.en: Now the base of a summertime outdoor cinema, you can view the remains of the reservoir that was the terminus of an aqueduct that transported water for Roman-era Athenians from Parnitha to the base of Mount Lycabettus. You can only peer through windows and are not able to descend into the reservoir.

stops.name: Hellenic Parliament Building
stops.en: This building is on the eastern side of the square. It was the former royal palace before Greece became a republic. At its base, facing the square, is the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier.

stops.name: Benaki Museum of Islamic Art
stops.en: An excellent collection which anyone interested in Islamic art will want to see. The museum was opened in 2004 as a branch of the Benaki, but is in a different part of town in two connected buildings.

stops.name: Park of Maritime Tradition
stops.en: Including the historical warships Georgios Averof, Velos and a replica of an ancient trireme.

stops.name: Εθνικό Αρχαιολογικό Μουσείο
stops.lc: Αυτό είναι το μεγαλυτερο και πιο γνωστό μουσείο της Αθήνας, και συχνά υπάρχει συνωστισμός. Η μεγάλη του συλλογή περιλαμβάνει εκθέματα απο τις Μυκήνες απο τις ανασκαφές του Χέινριχ Σλίμαν, περιλαμβανομένου των αρχαιώτερων Ελληνικών αγαλματιών του 2.000π.χ., τοιχογραφίες απο την Σαντορίνι, το μηχανισμό των Αντικυθήρων (ο αρχαιώτερος γνωστός υπολογιστής), και πολλά άλλα που συνιστάται στον επισκέπτη

stops.name: Παρθενώνας
stops.lc: Ο μεγαλύτερος ναός στην Ακρόπολη, αφιερωμένος στην θεά Αθηνά, αργότερα μετατράπηκε σε Εκκλησία και σε Τέμενος. Χτίστθηκε μετάξυ 447 και 438 π.χ. στην κορύφωση της κλασικής περιόδου. Απο τον παρθενώνα αφεραίθηκαν τα "Ελγίνια Μάρμαρα" που βρίσκονται στο Βρετανικό Μουσείο στο Λονδίνο

stops.name: Ναός της Αθηνάς Νίκης
stops.lc: Ο πρώτος ναός στην Ακρόπολη που κτίσθηκε σε Ιωνικό ρυθμό

stops.name: Ερέχθειο
stops.lc: Αφιερωμένο στην λατρεία των δύο βασικών θεών της Αθήνας, την Αθηνά και τον Ποσειδώνα

stops.name: Ωδείο Ηρόδοτου Αττικού
stops.lc: Το αρχαίο θέατρο χρησιμοποιείται ακόμα και σήμερα για συναυλίες και παραστάσεις

stops.name: Ρωμαϊκή Αγορά
stops.lc: Στο δυτικό άκρο της Πλάκας, περιλαμβάνει έναν οκτάγωνο πύργο με διαφορετική θεότητα στην κάθε πλευρά, και τα μνημεία της αρχαίας αγοράς.

stops.name: Αρχαία Αγορά
stops.lc: Στο δυτικό άκρο της Πλάκας, διασχίζουμε την οδό Ανδριανού δυτικά της Βιβλιοθήκης του Ανδριανού. Ο Ναός του Ηφαίστου του 5ου π.χ. αιώνα βρίσκεται εδώ, η Στοά του Αττάλου έχει μετατραπεί σε μουσείο με ευρήματα απο της περιοχή της αγοράς. Κοντά στην αγορά βρίσκεται και μια απο τις αρχαιότερες εκλησίες της Αθήνας, οι Αγίοι Απόστολοι του 11ου αιώνα.

stops.name: Νέο μουσείο Ακρόπολης
stops.lc: Σχεδιασμένο απο τον Ελβετό αρχιτέκτονα Μπερνάντ Τσούμι, νότια της Ακρόπολης. Προσβαση απο τον σταθμό μετρό Ακρόπολης

stops.name: Μουσείο Μπενάκι Ισλαμικής τέχνης
stops.lc: Μια υπέροχη έκθεση που πρέπει να δει ο κάθε ενδιαφερόμενος στην Ισλαμική τέχνη. Το μουσείο άνοιξε το 2004 σας ένα τμήμα του μουσείου Μπενάκι.

stops.name: Μουσείο Κανελλόπουλου
stops.lc: Ένα μικρό μουσείο με εκθέματα απο τις Μυκήνες και Περσικά κοσμίματα.

stops.name: Μουσείο Ελληνικών μουσικών οργάνων
stops.lc: Εκθέτονται παραδοσιακά μουσικά όργανα με ηχογραφήσεις για τα περισσότερα απο αυτά

stops.name: Λαογραφικό μουσείο
stops.lc: Κοσμήματα, εργαλεία, λαϊκές ζωγραφιές, κεραμικά και στοιχεία εσωτερικής διακόσμισης, είναι μερικά απο τα εκθέματα, με πολλές παραδοσιακές φορεσίες. Πολύ καλό μουσείο στην κατηγορία του.

stops.name: Εθνικό Θέατρο
stops.lc: Ένα χαμηλό κτίριο που κτίσθηκε μεταξύ 1882 και 1890 σε σχέδια του αρχιτέκτονα Ένστ Ζίλλερ κατά παραγγελία του Βασιλειά Γεωργίου Α.

stops.name: Πινακοθήκη
stops.lc: Πίνακες απο Έλληνες ζωγράφους στο δεύτερο του εικοστού αιώνα

stops.name: πάρκο Ναυτικής Ιστορίας
stops.lc: Το θωρηκτό Αβέρωφ που βρίσκεται αγκυροβολημένο στη μαρίνα του Φλοίσβου (Τροκαντερό) και συγκεκριμένα δίπλα στο πάρκο Ναυτικής Ιστορίας, χρησιμοποιείται σήμερα σαν μουσείο.

stops.name: Μονή Πεντέλης της Κοιμήσεως της Θεοτόκου
stops.lc: Η Μονή Πεντέλης της Κοιμήσεως της Θεοτόκου είναι ιστορική μονή που βρίσκεται στην Πεντέλη. Κτίστηκε το 1578 από τον Άγιο Τιμόθεο Επισκόπου Ευβοίας που κατάγονταν από την Αττική, και που είχε φύγει από την έδρα του εξαιτίας διωμού του από τους Τούρκους. Η Μονή κυρήχτηκε σταυροπηγιακή και παραμένει μέχρι σήμερα. Άκμασε τον 17ο αιώνα με περίπου 100 μοναχούς, που ζούσαν κοινοβιακώς και διατηρούσαν πλο

stops.name: Μουσείο Βορρέ
stops.lc: Το Μουσείο Βορρέ ιδρύθηκε το 1983 και είναι ένα διαχρονικό μουσείο λαϊκής και σύγχρονης τέχνης στην Παιανία της ανατολικής Αττικής. Διαθέτει έκταση άνω των 18 στρεμμάτων στα οποία υπάρχουν διάφορα κτήρια, κήποι και αυλές, τα οποία κατανέμονται ανάμεσα στις συλλογές της λαογραφίας και της σύγχρονης ελληνικής τέχνης. Στις εγκαταστάσεις του περιλαμβάνονται πάνω από 6000 εκθέματα τα οποία καλύπτουν μι

eats.name: Σουβλάκι Κώστας 1950 συνταγμα (Kostas)
eats.note: It's authentic, friendly and fast.

eats.name: The 2 Brothers
eats.note: The best souvlaki in this part of Athens.

eats.name: Vegan Beat Athens
eats.note: Vegan street food restaurant. Tasty food and nice people that work there. A good place for all vegans and even non-vegans. The true Parthenon of the vegan scene of Athens. Excellent vegan souvlaki.

eats.name: The Traditional
eats.note: Traditional Greek food. If you want to eat in a quality village tavern in the center of Athens, you will come here. Great roasted food, salads and appetizers! The food is handmade.

eats.name: Krasopoulio tou Kokkora
eats.note: Among the best traditional Greek restaurants in Athens downtown. The owner is smiling, polite and very keen to assist. A wonderful casual lunch or dinner spot. Fresh ingredients and substantial portio

eats.name: Aspro Alogo
eats.note: An excellent little Greek restaurant well worth finding. Everything is fresh and delicious and the service is great. The owner is a helpful and generous guy. Attentive and familiar treatment.

eats.name: Atlantikos
eats.note: Nice little place with great seafood selection. The meals look simple and are delicious. The portions are quite large and the quality price ratio is very well balanced. One should go in time and expec

eats.name: Kafeneio Ivis
eats.note: Very authentic Greek tavern, frequented by locals. Great value for money. Warm welcome, nice terrace and fast service.

eats.name: Lefka
eats.note: A long-established traditional taverna with spacious outdoor seating. Closed Sundays.

eats.name: K Filippou
eats.note: A long-established taverna serving some of the best and most authentic food in Athens. Seating is indoors and outdoors, though it's hard to find a seat in the latter during pleasant weather.

eats.name: Karamanlidika
eats.note: A very remarkable, slightly upscale restaurant specializing in dishes native to the Karamanli people. Owing to their history, the food served here is a (very well-executed) mix between Greek and Turki

eats.name: Karavitis
eats.note: a severely traditional taverna where the speciality is stamnaki, or beef, potatoes and cheese cooked in tomato sauce in an individual clay pot. The fried zucchini here are also always good. Mostly pat

eats.name: Το Κιούπι (To Kioupi)
eats.note: Known among some expatriates as "the hole in the ground," this is a basement taverna serving authentic, inexpensive traditional Greek fare.

eats.name: Platanos Taverna
eats.note: One of the oldest tavernas in Plaka with a pleasant outdoor terrace under a huge plane tree, though some old Athens hands have complained that the food has become lacklustre.

eats.name: Zeus Xenios
eats.note: literally in the shadow of the Acropolis, offers quieter and less expensive dining than the many touristy tavernas lining Mnesikleous whose touts will try to snare you as you walk up the hill. The vie

eats.name: Pame Psirri
eats.note: On Agii Anargiri square -- Psiri. A "mezedopolio" where local singers sing rempetika music.

eats.name: O Morias
eats.note: Greek restaurant

eats.name: Voskopoula (The Shepherdess)
eats.note: Greek restaurant

eats.name: Τaverna Μanolis
eats.note: Greek restaurant taverna.

eats.name: Rosalia
eats.note: A tavern that serves simple, traditional Greek meals.

eats.name: Giántes
eats.note: A tavern with a garden serving organic dishes.

eats.name: Orea Penteli
eats.note: Another "mezedopolio" with live music in an old restored building.

eats.name: Cafe Avissinia
eats.note: A remarkable restaurant, serving refined and creative innovations on traditional Greek dishes in a chic setting. It is on the square of the same name which is the venue of the main Athens flea market.

eats.name: Balux
eats.note: One of the best bars in Athens for the specific style, to call it a bar is an understatement. Balux is large complex set right on the water in Glyfada, one of the trendiest areas of the city. It is op

eats.name: Rebetiki Istoria
eats.note: One of the best rebetica clubs, often open in summer when most others are closed.

eats.name: Ydria
eats.note: This sprawling cafe-restaurant that takes up a large part of Platía Paliás Agorás along Adhrianoú St. at the western end of Plaka, is a good place for daytime coffee or a before or after dinner drink.

eats.name: Costa
eats.note: Standard stuff, but has a nice air conditioned and quiet upstairs seating area overlooking the square.

eats.name: Metamatic_taf
eats.note: Independent space organising and hosting cultural events related to all forms of artistic production, and a point of social gathering. Great cocktails and a variety of jazz/soul music.

eats.name: Playce
eats.note: A really nice cafe where you can play board games whilst drinking your coffee. Very popular.

eats.name: Filion Cafe
eats.note: Start the day with a double shot of dark espresso at this cafe in the Kolonaki neighbourhood, just north of Syntagma Square.

eats.name: Μπαρμπά Γιάννης
eats.note: Παραδοσιακή απλή ταβέρνα, δημοφιλής στους φοιτητές, ανοιχτά όλη την ημέρα.

eats.name: Λέφκα
eats.note: Παραδοσιακή ταβέρνα και μεγάλη αυλή. Κλειστά την Κυριακή

eats.name: Ιντεάλ
eats.note: Ένα εστιατόριο όπου συχνάζουν οι εργαζόμενοι κατά το μεσημεριανο τους διάλλειμα, καλό να πάτε πριν το μεσημεριανό διάλλειμα

eats.name: Ροζαλία
eats.note: Ταβέρνα με παραδοσιακά απλά Ελληνικά πιάτα

eats.name: Γάντες
eats.note: Ταβέρνα με αυλή

eats.name: Ρμπέτικη ΙστορίαRebetiki Istoria
eats.note: Ένα απο τα ρεμπετάδικα, ανοιχτά και το καλοκαίρι

eats.name: Ο Χριστόφορος
eats.note: Ψησταριά, Τεράστιες μερίδες

eats.name: Μουρούζης
eats.note: Ψησταριά, Τεράστιες μερίδες

next.name: Evvia
next.note: Evia, or Euboea, is the second-largest Greek island in area and population, after Crete, and in close proximity to Athens. In less than 1.5 hours by bus, train, or car, you can reach Chalkis, or Halkida, the island's capital city and enjoy the local beaches, O

next.name: Sounio
next.note: Sounio, Ktel bus starts from central Athens and also stop in some areas in south Athens. 1 hour from central Athens by car.

next.name: Corinth
next.note: Day trips to the Corinth Canal, the ancient theatre at Epidaurus and to the ancient sites of Olympia, Delphi and Mycenae are easy with a rental car.

next.name: Peloponnese
next.note: Towns along the Peloponnese such as Nafplion are charming and worthwhile.
